correct_completion: she would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: Had she studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: she might have passed the exam.
she could have passed the exam.

options.text: she passes the exam every year.
options.why_wrong: The simple present describes a habit and does not express the unreal past result that 'Had she studied harder' sets up.

options.text: she would have passed the exam.
she will pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: The future tense describes a real future event. The stem signals an unreal past situation, so the result must be past-oriented.

options.text: she had passed the exam already.
options.why_wrong: The past perfect describes a completed fact, not the hypothetical result of a condition that did not happen.

explanation: Inverted conditionals drop 'if' and move 'had' to the front of the clause. The result clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle to match an unreal past condition.
